text: This chunk describes the symptoms of cholera, ranging from mild to severe. Mild cases involve minor symptoms like abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, with loose or watery stools not exceeding 1 liter per day, typically resolving within 1-3 days. Severe cases are characterized by profuse, watery diarrhea without abdominal pain, often projectile, accompanied by vomiting. The stool may initially contain solid matter and appear yellow, later becoming clear with a fishy odor. Severe cases can lead to rapid dehydration and shock within 4-18 hours if not treated promptly, potentially resulting in death.
